_readme: 8VC's cross-investor rulings for COLLECTION.md invariant 10 (same schema as data/collection/cross-investor.json; merged by verify at read time). `distinct`: name-key collisions that are different companies. `accepted`: real disagreements whose fix belongs to the wave alignment, because the stale side is another investor's file and §12 forbids editing it from this session. Six of the nineteen disagreements this run raised were resolved by ADOPTING the sibling's cited value (Erebor, Wispr Flow, Honor, and earlier Anduril, Cognition, Vercel, Ramp, Saronic, Commure, Asana, Hims, Yugabyte, Generalist, NewLimit, The Boring Company) — invariant 10 working exactly as intended: a sibling's published citation is cheaper and better than a fresh search, and it is what keeps one company reading the same way across the whole track record. Accepted entries are written as PAIRS, not as groups: verify matches a disagreement row-pair at a time, and a three-row group silently matches none of them.

accepted.reason: Rule A (Erik, 2026-09-06), which postdates both sibling runs. The $1.5B those rows publish is sourced to Tracxn, a data VENDOR, and Rule A says a vendor mark never bands a row: Airbyte's 2021 Series B was widely reported at that figure but the company published no post-money. 8VC's row records below_1b with the check. The fix is to re-run Rule A over the sibling rows at wave alignment, not to align 8VC's side up to an aggregator figure.
